title: "My name is... my name is...": A Linguistic Map for Voice Agents — Midam Kim, ServiceNow
talk_summary: A ServiceNow ML engineer presents a linguistic framework (sounds, words, interaction, mental model across listening/speaking channels) for diagnosing voice-agent failures, illustrated by a bot mangling her name and cutting her off. It is a conceptual/diagnostic taxonomy for voice UX, not an engineering technique for text-based agent orchestration.

takeaways.technique: Layered failure taxonomy for diagnosing agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: They decompose a failed interaction into interdependent layers (input recognition, understanding, turn timing, shared mental model) and attribute each failure to a specific layer rather than treating it as one opaque 'bad run'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's an SCT failure in the listening level... the STT did not recognize the word unit correctly, so it cuts me off

takeaways.technique: Track a persistent 'mental model' across a session, not just raw history
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue the durable artifact of an interaction is the accumulated shared mental model, while raw utterances vanish; the system should maintain and update that model dynamically over the timeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sounds, words, interactions vanish the moment they're spoken, but the mental model proceeds and grows over the timeline
